billboard <- read_csv("billboard.csv",

                            ))

audio_features <- read_csv("audio_features.csv", 
                           col_types = cols(song_id = col_skip(), 
                            performer = col_skip(), 
                            song = col_skip(), 
                            time_signature = col_skip(), 
                            spotify_track_preview_url = col_skip(),
                            spotify_track_explicit = col_skip(),
                            spotify_track_album = col_skip(),
                            spotify_track_id = col_skip()
                            ))

audio_features <- as_tibble(audio_features)
audio_features <- na.omit(audio_features)

```{r}
# Step 1: Rimuovi caratteri indesiderati
audio_features$spotify_genre <- gsub("\\[|\\]|'", "", audio_features$spotify_genre)

# Step 2: Creare una lista di generi separati da virgola
audio_features$spotify_genre <- strsplit(audio_features$spotify_genre, split = ",")

# Step 3: Estrarre solo il primo genere per ogni riga
audio_features$first_genre <- sapply(audio_features$spotify_genre, function(x) x[1])

audio_features$first_genre <- sapply(audio_features$spotify_genre, function(x) {
  if (length(x) == 0) {
    return("others")
  } else {
    return(x[1])
  }
})

a='
audio_features$spotify_track_popularity <- sapply(audio_features$spotify_track_popularity, function(x) {
  if (x <= 25) {
    return("low")
  }
  if (x > 25 & x <= 50) {
    return("medium")
  }
  if (x > 50 & x <= 75) {
    return("high")
  }
    if (x > 75 & x <= 100) {
    return("very high")
  } 
})
'
```

```{r}
# Conta la frequenza di ciascun valore nella colonna 'first_genre'
genre_counts <- table(audio_features$first_genre)

# Identifica i generi con meno di 50 occorrenze
low_count_genres <- names(genre_counts[genre_counts < 200])

# Sostituisci i generi con meno di 50 occorrenze con "others"
audio_features$first_genre <- ifelse(audio_features$first_genre %in% low_count_genres, "others", audio_features$first_genre)

# Ricontrolla le frequenze dopo il raggruppamento
genre_counts_after_grouping <- table(audio_features$first_genre)
audio_features <- subset(audio_features, select = -c(spotify_genre))
```

```{r}
# 1. Assicurati di usare la colonna aggiornata
df <- data.frame(first_genre = audio_features$first_genre)

# 2. Crea i dummy variables (one-hot encoding)
dummy <- dummyVars(~ first_genre, data = df)
final_df <- data.frame(predict(dummy, newdata = df))  # <- Qui dovevi usare final_df

# 3. Unisci con il dataset originale
audio_features_encoded <- bind_cols(
  audio_features %>% select(-first_genre),
  final_df
)
```

```{r}
# Seleziona solo le variabili numeriche
numeric_data <- audio_features %>%
  select(where(is.numeric))

# Calcola la matrice di correlazione
cor_matrix <- cor(numeric_data, use = "complete.obs")

ggcorrplot(cor_matrix, 
           method = "circle",      # o "square"
           type = "lower",         # solo triangolo inferiore         
           colors = c("red", "white", "blue"),  # come in seaborn
           title = "Matrice di Correlazione",
           ggtheme = ggplot2::theme_minimal())
```
```{r}
audio_features_encoded
```

```{r}

set.seed(45)
split <- initial_split(audio_features_encoded, prop = 0.8)
train_data <- training(split)
test_data  <- testing(split)

# 1. Prepara il recipe (già fatto)
recipe_spec <- recipe(spotify_track_popularity ~ ., data = train_data)

task = 'regression'

# 2. Definisci i modelli
models <- list(
  rf = rand_forest(mtry = 5) %>% set_engine("randomForest") %>% set_mode(task),
  #lm = linear_reg() %>% set_engine("lm") %>% set_mode(task),
  xgb = boost_tree(trees = 1000, tree_depth = 10) %>% set_engine("xgboost") %>% set_mode(task),
  knn = nearest_neighbor(neighbors = 5) %>% set_engine("kknn") %>% set_mode(task)
)

# 3. Crea una lista di workflow
workflows_list <- purrr::map(models, ~ workflow() %>% add_model(.x) %>% add_recipe(recipe_spec))

# 4. Fitta tutti i modelli
fitted_models <- purrr::map(workflows_list, ~ fit(.x, data = train_data))

# 5. Valuta su test set
results <- purrr::map(fitted_models, ~ {
  predict(.x, test_data) %>%
    bind_cols(test_data) %>%
    metrics(truth = spotify_track_popularity, estimate = .pred)
})

# 6. Combina risultati in una tabella leggibile
results_df <- bind_rows(results, .id = "model")

results_df %>%
  filter(.metric == "rmse") %>%
  arrange(.estimate)

print(results_df)
```


```{r}
results <- list()

for (model_name in names(fitted_models)) {
  model <- models[[model_name]]
  
  wf <- workflow() %>%
    add_model(model) %>%
    add_recipe(recipe_spec)
  
  fit_model <- fit(wf, data = train_data)
  
  preds <- predict(fit_model, test_data) %>%
    bind_cols(test_data) %>%
    mutate(model = model_name)
  
  results[[model_name]] <- preds
}

# Unione di tutte le predizioni
all_predictions <- bind_rows(results)

```

```{r}

ggplot(all_predictions, aes(x = spotify_track_popularity, y = .pred)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~model, scales = "free") +
  labs(
    title = "Predizioni vs Valori Reali per Modello",
    x = "Valori Reali (spotify_track_popularity)",
    y = "Predizioni"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
